title: I.7: Fugue in Eb major

groocock.chapter: 7 Group 2: Fugues for Three Voices, without Stretto

entries.notes: tonal answer to a modulating subject; drop of a tone at the rest; whole answer in the tonic key
countersubject in middle modified during the semiquaver run of bar 6
begins at last note of bar 10; retains original tonality
beginning of CS in middle slightly varied (diagram shows (C))
enters at last note of bar 25; restores tonic
begins at end of bar 28 as if answer in IV; after the rest in bar 29 proves to be subject; combines shapes of subject and answer and incorporates the tied note of the CS
enters end of bar 33; chromatic adornment in bar 34

episodes.material: main idea (not exact notes) of the codetta; soprano alludes to subject leaps and CS tied-note rhythm
codetta figure in imitation bass/soprano, middle by augmentation; bar 10 bass develops codetta figure, upper voices allude to CS by diminution
begins with interchange of most of episode 2; from bar 15 soprano develops codetta figure
variant of first half of subject in soprano, allusions to subject and codetta; pattern changes to rising sequence (text says "at bar 21"); CS material in bars 24-25
continues pattern of second half of episode 5
varied repetition of episode 2 with upper voices interchanged

codettas.notes: modulates back from V to I; its figure is the main material of the fugue

countersubjects.first: second note of bar 3 (soprano), ends with last note of the answer
countersubjects.notes: must be moved up a tone to fit the subject (done in the semiquaver run of bar 6); one or other form used with all but two later entries; free part (not a second CS) at bar 6, different in each of four later entries. Interchange interval from list p.13

subject.answer: tonal; answer to a modulating subject (drop of a tone at the rest; semitone becomes minor third)
subject.notes: subject starts on dominant and modulates I-V; whole answer in tonic because codetta re-establishes I, answer is tonal, and CS uses notes of tonic key (pp.8, 35)

key_plan: Group 2 table: Exp I-V I EP I-V | EP I | Dev EP vi EP vi-iii | Final EP I EP I-V EP I

claims.claim: About 65% of the fugue is not directly concerned with subject or answer but with development of figures from subject, CS and especially the codetta of bar 2.
Choice of subject or answer form controls tonality: subject form at bar 20 modulates vi-iii; answer at 25 restores tonic.
Exposition has a codetta (bar 2) and an episode before the third entry (bars 4-5).
Redundant entry of the answer at bar 10.
Entry at bar 28 combines shapes of subject and answer and incorporates the tied note of the CS.
